The flagship is Microsoft 365 Copilot, introduced in early 2023, which embeds GPT-4 (and newer models) into Office apps. This means users can ask natural-language questions in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and get AI-generated drafts, summaries, or analyses that leverage the user’s actual documents and data. Separately, GitHub Copilot (launched 2021) is a coding assistant in IDEs like VS Code or JetBrains, suggesting code completions and generating functions. In 2025, Microsoft bridged these under a unified branding and expanded features: it released Copilot Chat for Business, a standalone chat interface powered by GPT-4 (free tier for employees) ([18] www.reuters.com), and continued updating both M365 and developer Copilots. Key characteristics include deep integration with Microsoft tools, a multi-model backend, and enterprise management via Azure Active Directory and Viva Insights.
Models & Architecture: While initially built on OpenAI’s GPT-4, Microsoft’s Copilot platform now uses a mix of models.
According to company reports, it is “customizing and training its own models, such as Phi-4” and gradually adding third-party models ([14] www.reuters.com). By late 2025, Copilot services allow administrators to select among model families: Microsoft offers GPT variants (including the newest GPT-5 codex models), Anthropic’s Claude (Opus 4.1, Sonnet 4.5), Google’s Gemini (up to Gemini 2.5 Pro) ([2] www.itpro.com) ([3] www.windowscentral.com), and Microsoft’s own LLMs.
For example, GitHub Copilot Enterprise explicitly deprecated older GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 mini models, urging migration to GPT-5 and Claude 4.1 ([2] www.itpro.com). This multi-model approach lets customers balance cost, performance, and governance. Under the hood, Copilot often uses adapted GPT models fine-tuned with Microsoft’s data (through Azure’s infrastructure), but crucially like ChatGPT, Microsoft states it does not use customer content for LLM training ([27] www.reuters.com) ([14] www.reuters.com).
Integration in Office (Microsoft 365 Copilot): In the Microsoft 365 suite, Copilot is a sidebar/chat UI in applications. In Word it can generate document drafts or rewrite text; in Excel it can summarize tables or write formulas based on a natural query; in Outlook it drafts emails; in Teams/OneNote/SharePoint it can take meeting summaries or extract action items. All Copilot interactions can draw on organizational context via Microsoft Graph (e.g. pulling data from mail, calendar, files) so responses are personalized to the company’s data. Notably, Copilot in Excel can act on the actual spreadsheet content: an upcoming Beta feature allows users to enter plain-English prompts as worksheet formulas to analyze or visualize data ([35] www.windowscentral.com). This “Excel COPILOT function” (rolling out as a beta in mid-2025) exemplifies the tight spreadsheet integration. Microsoft is also extending Copilot to Windows itself: in Windows 11´s August 2025 update, “Copilot Vision” lets the assistant interpret on-screen content when a user shares their app window ([36] www.windowscentral.com). Moreover, Copilot has gained a semblance of memory: new updates (Oct 2025) enable tracking of user preferences and past interactions across sessions ([37] www.reuters.com), which mirrors ChatGPT’s memory feature.
Integration for Developers (GitHub Copilot): GitHub Copilot is integrated into IDEs (VS Code, JetBrains, GitHub Codespaces) and provides inline code completions, autogenerated code snippets, and a chat box for asking coding questions. It leverages OpenAI codex models and now GPT-5-codex models, as well as optionally Claude or Gemini ([2] www.itpro.com) ([3] www.windowscentral.com). In 2025, GitHub introduced a public preview “agents panel” that lets developers delegate multi-step tasks to Copilot agents (e.g. “implement this feature across these repos”) ([38] www.itpro.com). This “mission control” UI automates routine dev chores. Additionally, Copilot Chat (released Jan 2025† ([18] www.reuters.com)) lets employees (with or without GitHub) spawn AI chatbots to assist on research, drafting, or analytic queries, using GPT-4 under a Microsoft interface. GitHub Copilot also features an evolving “Copilot Studio” interface for managing settings and accessing previews. GitHub’s enterprise plan now offers SOC 2/ISO certifications for Copilot Business (code completion, in-IDE chat) (github.blog), signaling enterprise readiness.

Features & Capabilities: Copilot emphasizes business productivity and developer efficiency. In Copilot Chat (business tier), users can create on-demand AI agents for tasks like market research, document generation, or prep for meetings ([18] www.reuters.com). However, deeper integrations (e.g. automatically turning a Teams call transcript into slides) require the paid 365 Copilot subscription ([41] www.reuters.com). Unlike ChatGPT’s more open-ended chat design, Copilot’s UI and functions are guided by task-specific prompts in the context of each app. It offers summarization (e.g. summarizing threads/emails), data analysis in Excel, creative design in PowerPoint (remixing visuals), etc. Copilot also recently added co-authoring assistance features (e.g. collaborative Google app integration ([37] www.reuters.com)). Pricing & Licensing: Microsoft’s Copilot is sold mainly as an add-on seat-license on top of existing Microsoft 365 subscriptions. Historically announced at ~$30 per user per month for the premium Copilot Chat for Teams/Office ([41] www.reuters.com), with separate plans for GitHub Copilot. Enterprise customers often commit at scale (Barclays covers 100k seats ([10] www.techradar.com)). In contrast to ChatGPT Enterprise’s flat-fee per organization, Microsoft’s model is strictly per-seat. GitHub Copilot Business costs per developer seat. Microsoft’s inclusive bundling (some deals include Copilot features) complicates exact comparisons, but overall Copilot requires substantial subscription investment beyond existing Office licensing.
Limitations and Criticism: Users and industry analysts have noted shortcomings in Copilot. Some early adopters found Copilot Chat (Bing Chat) responses less reliable than ChatGPT’s ([43] www.windowscentral.com); “Merciless performance inconsistencies” led even Microsoft staff to prefer ChatGPT’s quality ([44] www.windowscentral.com). Developers have protested when Copilot features are auto-enabled (e.g. Chat and AI suggestions in GitHub issues/Pull Requests), calling them disruptive and a potential IP risk ([45] www.techradar.com). The Microsoft culture of caution (“trauma” from Clippy) has slowed some aggressive AI innovation, critics say ([44] www.windowscentral.com). Moreover, because Copilot reaches into core business data, misconfigurations can expose confidential content (as Concentric’s report highlighted ([39] www.techradar.com)). Microsoft is actively iterating to address these issues (introducing training and documentation via Copilot Academy, adding privacy guards), but enterprises must balance Copilot’s benefits with concerns about overreach, accuracy, and integration complexity.

Recent developments also reflect regulatory alignment: OpenAI will store UK user data locally under a UK government partnership ([28] www.reuters.com), and the EU’s AI Act now treats general-purpose AI (like ChatGPT and Copilot) under rigorous transparency standards ([15] apnews.com) ([54] www.reuters.com). Enterprises will have to factor these into their deployments.
Cost Analysis: Pricing comparisons are complex. ChatGPT Enterprise is typically negotiated (OpenAI’s website suggests enterprise pricing with volume discounts but no public per-user rate). Microsoft’s $30/month/per-seat price for 365 Copilot functions ([41] www.reuters.com) is concrete. For a 100-seat company, that’s $36,000/year, comparable to some CRM or analytics tools. However, Microsoft often bundles Copilot with broader licensing or offers it via enterprise agreements. GitHub Copilot Business costs about $10–15 per developer per month (depending on region and plan). ChatGPT Enterprise claims unlimited GPT-4 usage; Copilot usage is bounded by subscription tier (basic Copilot Chat free, premium features paywalled). There have been complaints about Microsoft’s additional charges (e.g. needing premium subscription to summarise Teams calls) ([41] www.reuters.com), whereas ChatGPT treats its advanced reasoning as included. In sum, Microsoft’s approach is granular (pay per user per feature) while OpenAI’s is a flat enterprise model with some tiers.
Feature Efficacy: Several benchmarks and anecdotes compare output quality. Industry commentary suggests ChatGPT often outperforms Copilot Chat: WindowsCentral reported Microsoft’s internal experience that employees “prefer paying out-of-pocket for ChatGPT” due to better answers ([43] www.windowscentral.com).
GitHub Copilot remains widely regarded as improving developer speed (average studies show 30–40% faster coding with Copilot suggestions), but some code reviews found occasional security or style issues in AI-generated code. In office tasks, Microsoft claims Copilot saves hours in tasks like crafting slides or analyzing numbers, but user feedback on those claims remains mixed. In any case, both products are advancing rapidly: planned updates like Copilot’s multi-user storytelling and ChatGPT’s enhanced browsing will blur functional gaps ([37] www.reuters.com) ([16] www.tomsguide.com).
Implications and Future Directions Enterprise Workflow Transformation: Both ChatGPT and Copilot are catalysts for rethinking work. They enable employees to interact with software in natural language rather than complex interfaces, democratizing access to data analysis and automation. We are seeing the beginnings of a new class of “AI literate” job roles, where understanding how to prompt-engineer or manage AI agents is a professional skill. Surveys indicate employees feel more creative and efficient with these tools, though many also express uncertainty about errors. For organizations, the ability to rapidly prototype processes with AI (e.g. building a ChatGPT agent to onboard new hires) reduces dev overhead. At the same time, these tools necessitate new policies: companies now need AI governance frameworks (to audit outputs for compliance, to train staff on data hygiene, etc.).
Competitive Landscape: The ChatGPT vs Copilot contest is also a proxy for OpenAI vs Microsoft (and their partners). Microsoft’s move to integrate Anthropic and Google models into Copilot suggests a conscious strategy to avoid vendor lock-in ([14] www.reuters.com) ([2] www.itpro.com). Amazon, Salesforce, and others are launching their own copilots, adding competitive pressure. OpenAI’s partnership with SAP in Germany (“OpenAI for Germany”) marks authorities vying to shape AI platforms for their markets ([51] www.techradar.com).
Meanwhile, model innovation continues rapidly: GPT-5’s launch brought capabilities like integrated code execution and advanced reasoning ([16] www.tomsguide.com), and competitors (Meta’s Llama, Anthropic’s Claude IntuitionLabs - AI Software for Pharma & Biotech ChatGPT vs. Copilot: An Enterprise Feature Comparison (2025) © 2026 IntuitionLabs.ai - North America's Leading AI Software Development Firm for Pharmaceutical & Biotech. Future Features: The pipeline of enhancements is rich. On the ChatGPT side, beyond “company knowledge” and memory, OpenAI is exploring multi-modal agents that can plan tasks autonomously (e.g. connect multiple APIs to complete an assignment). The developer conference in Oct 2025 emphasized apps integration (Spotify, Zillow, etc.) via new APIs ([55] www.reuters.com), effectively turning ChatGPT into a platform for enterprise app automation. We may expect ChatGPT to become an “operating system” layer across business software, as OpenAI CEO implies ([13] www.reuters.com).
Microsoft’s roadmap includes deeper Office integration (e.g. tighter integration with Dynamics CRM or Azure services), richer developer workflows (Copilot in GitHub Actions and CLI), and system-wide AI (as seen with Windows Copilot features ([36] www.windowscentral.com)). Notably, Microsoft has previewed Copilot in Edge that can reason over open browser tabs, prefiguring a future where Copilot sits on the desktop rather than just in apps ([47] www.reuters.com). Both companies are also investing in AI safety research, to make their copilots more reliable and explainable; for instance, new benchmarks penalize overconfident answers to reduce hallucination ([19] www.tomsguide.com).
Strategic Considerations for Enterprises: Businesses must weigh ChatGPT vs Copilot based on use case and ecosystem. Companies already invested in Microsoft (Office 365, Windows, Azure) may find Copilot’s seamless integration attractive. Firms needing a broad, platform-agnostic solution or with hybrid environments might lean on ChatGPT’s flexibility and large model scale. Some will likely use both: example, using ChatGPT for external customer bots and Copilot within Outlook/Excel. Cost planning is critical: ChatGPT’s “unlimited GPT-4” can simplify budgeting for heavy users, whereas Copilot’s per-seat fees can balloon if adopted by many.
Regulators are already taking interest. The EU’s voluntary code of practice (mid-2025) calls for transparency from “general purpose AI” systems like these ([15] apnews.com). OpenAI and Microsoft have pledged to comply (e.g. by listing credit sources for answers and allowing audits of model training data). Data residency laws (like those emerging in UK, Germany) mean cloud deployment choices will matter. One recent development: Microsoft added a Copilot feature to track internal AI usage and even benchmark against competitors ([40] www.itpro.com), acknowledging that businesses want metrics on AI ROI and compliance.
Conclusion In the span of just a few years, generative AI assistants have moved from novelty to enterprise staples. ChatGPT Enterprise and Microsoft Copilot are at the forefront, each offering powerful AI productivity gains while navigating challenges of accuracy, security, and integration. ChatGPT provides a versatile, open platform with cutting-edge models and broad interoperability ([1] www.techradar.com) ([4] www.techradar.com); Microsoft Copilot leverages trusted enterprise apps with a deep ecosystem tie-in and now a diverse model portfolio ([14] www.reuters.com) ([2] www.itpro.com). Data indicates massive adoption across industries (from financial firms to government agencies) and overwhelmingly positive reports of efficiency improvements, though tempered by concerns over data exposure ([39] www.techradar.com) ([45] www.techradar.com).
Looking ahead, we anticipate the gap between these platforms to narrow as they adopt each other’s strengths: ChatGPT is building tighter internal data links and control features, while Copilot is opening up to multiple AI engines and user-driven automation. Enterprises will benefit from both competition and convergence: more choice of AI tools that suit specific workflows. However, organizations must also prepare for evolving governance: ensuring human oversight of AI outputs, securing sensitive data, and aligning with new regulations.

## The Evolving Competitive Landscape

The GenAI market continues shifting rapidly. Perplexity closed a $500 million funding round in June 2025 that elevated its valuation to $14 billion. The platform launched Comet, an AI-powered browser, and developed Shopping Hub with backing from Amazon and Nvidia.

Meanwhile, ChatGPT maintains its position as the most widely recognized AI platform with continuous model improvements. GPT-4o replaced GPT-4 as the default model and recent upgrades improved instruction following, problem solving, and conversational flow. [...] Perplexity interface.

Perplexity has established itself as a specialized contender in the crowded GenAI market by positioning itself primarily as an AI-powered search engine rather than a general-purpose chatbot. The platform processed 780 million search queries in May 2025 and attracted 153 million website visits, demonstrating significant market traction. Perplexity provides access to multiple advanced AI models including GPT-4o, Claude, and Llama 3.1 70B, automatically selecting the optimal model for each query. [...] ## ChatGPT: Versatility and Creative Excellence

ChatGPT’s GPT-5 release in August 2025 delivered substantial improvements in coding, instruction following, and long-context comprehension with support for up to 1 million tokens. The platform remains the most versatile GenAI tool, excelling across diverse applications from content creation to complex problem-solving.

### ChatGPT’s Advantages

Creative Writing and Content Generation: ChatGPT produces imaginative, stylistically nuanced content. When asked to write in specific styles or create original creative work, ChatGPT generates vivid, engaging material that captures voice and tone effectively.

## How Does Perplexity Compare Against Other GenAI Models?

[Copy link](/)

## Key Facts at a Glance

* **Citation System**: Perplexity provides numbered citations with direct source links for every response, enhancing verification and transparency
* **Real-Time Search**: Searches the web daily to deliver current information, unlike models with fixed knowledge cutoffs
* **Multi-Model Architecture**: Uses a model-routing framework that automatically selects between GPT-5, Claude 4.5, Mistral, and Gemini based on query complexity
* **Deep Research Mode**: Free for all users with unlimited queries for Pro subscribers
* **Processing Scale**: Handles over 100 million search queries weekly with a target of 1 billion weekly queries by end of 2025
* **Market Position**: Ranked #268 globally among websites with availability in 238 countries and 46 languages
* **Pricing**: Pro subscription at $20/month includes GPT-4 access, unlimited Deep Research, image generation, and increased query limits

Perplexity interface.

Perplexity has established itself as a specialized contender in the crowded GenAI market by positioning itself primarily as an AI-powered search engine rather than a general-purpose chatbot. The platform processed 780 million search queries in May 2025 and attracted 153 million website visits, demonstrating [significant market traction](https://www.index.dev/blog/perplexity-statistics). Perplexity provides access to multiple advanced AI models including GPT-4o, Claude, and Llama 3.1 70B, automatically selecting the [optimal model](https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10354919-what-advanced-ai-models-are-included-in-my-subscription) for each query.

Where Perplexity excels is citation transparency and real-time information retrieval. Every answer includes source citations with direct links, allowing users to [verify information](https://gitmind.com/what-is-perplexity.html) and explore original sources. This positions Perplexity between traditional search engines and conversational AI, offering a middle ground that prioritizes factual accuracy over creative versatility. The platform recently launched Deep Research, which performs dozens of searches and reads hundreds of sources to autonomously deliver comprehensive reports on complex topics.

## Perplexity’s Core Strengths Against Competitors

### Research Accuracy and Source Transparency

Perplexity’s primary advantage lies in research-oriented tasks. The platform pulls information from recent articles, indexes the web daily, and presents findings with complete source attribution. When asked factual questions requiring verification, Perplexity consistently delivers more reliable, traceable answers than general conversational models.

For academic researchers, journalists, and professionals requiring verifiable information, this citation system proves invaluable. Users can trace every claim back to its original source, assess source credibility, and explore topics more deeply through provided links. This transparency addresses one of the fundamental challenges facing GenAI: hallucination and unverifiable claims.

Perplexity’s Enterprise users access additional orchestration layers including retrieval agents for data collection, synthesis agents for structured insights, and verification agents that validate citations against live sources. This multi-agent framework has found deployment in finance, consulting, and education sectors for knowledge automation and compliance reporting.

### Real-Time Information Access

Unlike static AI models with knowledge cutoffs, Perplexity searches the web in real-time. For queries about current events, stock prices, recent technological developments, or breaking news, Perplexity maintains an accuracy advantage over competitors. The platform automatically determines when web search is necessary versus when existing knowledge suffices.

This capability makes Perplexity particularly effective for competitor analysis, news tracking, and monitoring specific topics. The platform launched over 75 features in 2025, including app connectors for Gmail, Notion, Linear, and GitHub, plus voice assistance for on-the-go queries.

### Speed and Conciseness

Perplexity optimizes for quick, direct answers. Rather than generating lengthy conversational responses, the platform provides condensed information with supporting sources. For users seeking fast fact-checking or straightforward answers without extended dialogue, this approach proves more efficient than conversational models.

## Where Perplexity Falls Short

### Creative Content Generation

Perplexity’s focus on factual accuracy comes at the expense of creative capabilities. When asked to generate poetry, fiction, or imaginative content, the platform produces functional but uninspired results. ChatGPT and Claude demonstrate substantially stronger creative writing abilities, capturing stylistic nuances and producing more evocative, engaging content.

### Conversational Depth and Personalization

Perplexity lacks the conversational warmth and personalized guidance that characterizes ChatGPT and Claude. When users seek tailored advice, step-by-step instructions with anticipatory guidance, or engaging dialogue, conversational models provide more satisfying experiences. Perplexity delivers information but doesn’t create the sense of collaboration or understanding that emerges from extended conversations with other models.

### Context Window Limitations

Perplexity’s smaller context window restricts its ability to handle lengthy or highly complex queries compared to competitors. For analyzing extensive documents, maintaining context across long conversations, or processing multiple interconnected topics simultaneously, Google Gemini’s million-token context window or Claude’s 200,000-token capacity offer superior performance.

### Image Generation and Multimodal Capabilities

While Perplexity Pro includes image generation features, these remain less developed than ChatGPT’s DALL-E integration or other specialized image generation tools. For projects requiring visual content creation, Perplexity offers basic functionality rather than advanced capabilities.

## ChatGPT: Versatility and Creative Excellence

ChatGPT’s GPT-5 release in August 2025 delivered substantial improvements in coding, instruction following, and long-context comprehension with support for up to 1 million tokens. The platform remains the most versatile GenAI tool, excelling across diverse applications from content creation to complex problem-solving.

### ChatGPT’s Advantages

**Creative Writing and Content Generation**: ChatGPT produces imaginative, stylistically nuanced content. When asked to write in specific styles or create original creative work, ChatGPT generates vivid, engaging material that captures voice and tone effectively.

**Conversational Intelligence**: GPT-4.5 and subsequent [GPT-5.1](https://www.sentisight.ai/how-is-chatgpt-5-1-different-to-the-past-model/) demonstrates improved emotional intelligence, understanding subtle cues and implicit expectations with greater nuance. The model adapts its responses based on context, inviting further conversation when appropriate or providing comprehensive information when needed.

**Multimodal Integration**: GPT-4o [combines](https://www.techtarget.com/whatis/feature/GPT-4o-explained-Everything-you-need-to-know) text, voice, and vision processing within a single unified model, enabling real-time verbal conversations without noticeable delays. This seamless integration across modalities creates more natural interaction patterns.

**Image Generation**: ChatGPT’s DALL-E integration provides sophisticated image creation capabilities directly within conversations, with automatic saving to a Library in the sidebar for easy browsing and reuse.

### ChatGPT’s Limitations

**Source Verification**: ChatGPT provides citations in search mode but historically struggles with source accuracy in standard conversation mode. Users must verify important factual claims independently.

**Occasional Hallucinations**: Despite improvements, ChatGPT can generate plausible-sounding but incorrect information, particularly on obscure topics or when pushed beyond its training data.

## Google Gemini: Integration and Analytical Power

Gemini’s latest version supports up to 1 million tokens of context and features improved long-context comprehension. The platform excels at handling complex, large-scale tasks requiring deep analysis.

### Gemini’s Strengths

**Google Ecosystem Integration**: For users embedded in Google Workspace, Gemini offers unmatched convenience. The platform accesses Gmail, Google Drive, and other services directly, streamlining workflows for professionals managing collaborative projects.

**Complex Data Processing**: Gemini handles extensive datasets and performs sophisticated document analysis efficiently. Its large context window allows processing hundreds of pages while maintaining coherent understanding.

**Reasoning Capabilities**: Gemini demonstrates strong performance in logic, deductive reasoning, and analytical tasks requiring systematic thinking.

### Gemini’s Weaknesses

**Formal Output Style**: Gemini’s responses often feel academic or formal, making it less suitable for casual communication or creative projects requiring personality and warmth.

**Limited Creative Flair**: While competent at analytical tasks, Gemini produces less imaginative, less stylistically varied content than ChatGPT or Claude.

## Claude AI: Strategic Thinking and Extended Context

Claude 3.7 Sonnet introduced hybrid reasoning capabilities with an “extended thinking mode” that makes its reasoning process visible to users. Claude focuses on brainstorming, creative writing, and strategic planning.

### Claude’s Competitive Advantages

**Natural Interaction Style**: Claude creates engaging, human-like conversations with warmth and personality. This makes extended interactions feel more natural than with other platforms.

**Strategic Creativity**: Claude excels at generating innovative ideas, exploring possibilities, and developing strategic plans. For brainstorming sessions or creative problem-solving, Claude provides thoughtful, well-developed perspectives.

**Large Context Window**: Claude’s 200,000-token context window enables analysis of lengthy documents and maintenance of coherent understanding across extended conversations.

**Safety and Ethics Focus**: Built with emphasis on ethical AI and safe interactions, Claude demonstrates reliability in applications requiring consistent, appropriate responses.

### Claude’s Limitations

**No Image Generation**: Claude lacks built-in image creation capabilities, limiting its utility for projects requiring visual content.

**Research Speed**: For quick fact-checking or real-time information needs, Claude’s approach feels slower than Perplexity’s focused search methodology.

## Performance Comparison Table

| Feature | Perplexity | ChatGPT | Gemini | Claude |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Citation Transparency | Excellent | Good (search mode) | Moderate | Moderate |
| Real-Time Information | Excellent | Good | Good | Limited |
| Creative Writing | Fair | Excellent | Good | Excellent |
| Conversational Depth | Fair | Excellent | Good | Excellent |
| Code Generation | Good | Excellent | Good | Good |
| Image Generation | Limited | Excellent | Moderate | None |
| Context Window | ~128k tokens | 1M tokens | 1M tokens | 200k tokens |
| Research Accuracy | Excellent | Good | Good | Good |
| Response Speed | Fast | Fast | Moderate | Moderate |
| Pricing (Pro) (slightly depends on region) | $20/month | $20/month | $20/month | $20/month |

## Which Model Serves Specific Use Cases Best?

**Academic Research and Fact-Checking**: Perplexity dominates this category with transparent citations, source verification, and real-time information access. Students, researchers, and journalists benefit most from this approach.

**Creative Writing and Content Creation**: ChatGPT and Claude tie for creative excellence. ChatGPT offers more versatility and image generation, while Claude provides more strategic, thoughtful creative development.

**Professional Document Analysis**: Google Gemini leads for users within the Google ecosystem, particularly those analyzing extensive datasets or collaborative documents across Google Workspace.

**Coding and Software Development**: ChatGPT’s GPT-4.1 leads SWE-bench Verified at 74.9% and shows particular strength in frontend coding with 80% preference in human grading comparisons.

**Strategic Planning and Brainstorming**: Claude excels at exploring possibilities, developing strategies, and maintaining extended analytical conversations.

**Quick Information Retrieval**: Perplexity delivers fastest results for straightforward factual queries requiring minimal conversation.

**Customer Service and Extended Dialogue**: ChatGPT and Claude both handle ongoing conversations effectively, with Claude showing slightly better emotional intelligence and ChatGPT offering more versatility.

## The Evolving Competitive Landscape

The GenAI market continues shifting rapidly. Perplexity closed a $500 million funding round in June 2025 that elevated its valuation to $14 billion. The platform launched Comet, an AI-powered browser, and developed Shopping Hub with backing from Amazon and Nvidia.

Meanwhile, ChatGPT maintains its position as the most widely recognized AI platform with continuous model improvements. GPT-4o replaced GPT-4 as the default model and recent upgrades improved instruction following, problem solving, and conversational flow.

No single model dominates all categories. The optimal choice depends on specific requirements: citation transparency, creative capability, ecosystem integration, or analytical depth. Many professionals maintain subscriptions to multiple platforms, selecting tools based on immediate task requirements.

## Future Trajectories

Perplexity targets 1 billion weekly queries by end of 2025, suggesting continued focus on search-oriented AI. The platform’s emphasis on verification and transparency addresses growing concerns about AI-generated misinformation.

ChatGPT continues expanding multimodal capabilities and reasoning abilities, positioning itself as the comprehensive general-purpose AI assistant. Google Gemini deepens integration with enterprise workflows, while Claude refines its strategic thinking and extended context capabilities.

The market appears moving toward specialization rather than one model conquering all use cases. Perplexity’s commitment to verified, cited information creates a distinct niche that conversational models don’t adequately address. For users prioritizing factual accuracy and source transparency, Perplexity offers capabilities that general-purpose chatbots struggle to match.

## Practical Recommendations

Start with the task at hand. For research requiring verification, begin with Perplexity. For creative projects, explore ChatGPT or Claude. For document analysis within Google Workspace, leverage Gemini. For coding, prioritize ChatGPT’s latest models.

Consider maintaining access to multiple platforms. Free tiers provide sufficient capability for casual use. Upgrade to paid subscriptions ($20/month across platforms) when frequency or advanced features justify the investment.

Verify important information regardless of source. Even Perplexity’s cited sources require evaluation for credibility, bias, and relevance. No AI platform eliminates the need for critical thinking and independent verification.

The choice between Perplexity and other GenAI models isn’t about identifying a universal winner. It’s about matching tools to tasks, recognizing each platform’s distinct strengths, and selecting appropriately for specific situations. Perplexity excels where verification matters most. Conversational models shine where creativity, versatility, and extended dialogue drive value.

# Comparing Online AI Tools in 2025: Grok, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, and Gemini

* [Report this article](/uas/login?session_redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.linkedin.com%2Fpulse%2Fcomparing-online-ai-tools-2025-grok-chatgpt-claude-jeff-3fkqe&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_ellipsis-menu-semaphore-sign-in-redirect&guestReportContentType=PONCHO_ARTICLE&_f=guest-reporting)

[Jeff Kikel](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jeffkikel) 

### Jeff Kikel

Published Jun 10, 2025

[+ Follow](https://www.linkedin.com/signup/cold-join?session_redirect=%2Fpulse%2Fcomparing-online-ai-tools-2025-grok-chatgpt-claude-jeff-3fkqe&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_publisher-author-card)

In 2025, artificial intelligence is no longer just a buzzword—it’s a vital tool for business success. From streamlining operations to uncovering market insights, AI assistants are helping leaders stay ahead in a competitive world. For business owners and C-suite executives, the challenge is picking the right AI tool from a crowded field. This article compares five leading options—Grok, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, and Gemini—based on six key factors: usability, research capabilities, creativity, integration with other tools, pricing, and real-time data access. With clear rankings and practical examples, you’ll see how each tool can serve your business needs.

### Why AI Matters for Your Business

AI tools are like having a super-smart assistant who never sleeps. They can analyze data, write reports, or even create marketing content in minutes. For busy executives, the best AI tools are easy to use, work with your existing software, and deliver fast, reliable results. But with so many choices, it’s tough to know where to start. That’s why we’ve broken down these five tools, scoring them on a 1-10 scale to help you decide which fits your goals.

### What We’re Comparing

We’re looking at six areas that matter most to business leaders:

* Usability: Is the tool simple to navigate?
* Research Capabilities: Can it find accurate, up-to-date information?
* Creativity: Does it help with writing, coding, or creative projects?
* Integration: Does it connect with software you already use?
* Pricing: What’s the cost, and what’s included in free or paid plans?
* Real-Time Data Access: Can it pull the latest data for quick decisions?

Let’s explore each tool and see how they stack up.

### Tool-by-Tool Breakdown

### Grok: The Real-Time Trend Tracker

Imagine having an AI that’s always plugged into the pulse of social media. Grok, built by xAI, is just that—a “truth-seeking” assistant that pulls real-time insights from the X platform. Its bold, witty tone makes it feel like a lively conversation partner. By June 2025, Grok has become a favorite for those who need unfiltered, up-to-the-minute information.

* Usability: Grok’s interface is clean and engaging, though it’s not as polished for corporate settings as some competitors. Score: 8/10
* Research Capabilities: With DeepSearch and DeeperSearch modes, Grok delivers quick, source-backed reports, perfect for tracking trends. Score: 9/10
* Creativity: It’s great for crafting catchy social media posts or bold content. Score: 8/10
* Integration: Works on web, iOS, Android, and X, with a developer API, but doesn’t connect deeply with business tools. Score: 7/10
* Pricing: Free for basic use, with SuperGrok at $30/month or X Premium plans starting at $8/month ([xAI](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=https%3A%2F%2Fx%2Eai%2Fgrok&urlhash=JYbK&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block)). Score: 9/10
* Real-Time Data Access: Unmatched, thanks to its X integration. Score: 10/10

Best Use Case: A social media manager monitoring viral trends or a journalist chasing breaking news will find Grok’s speed invaluable.

Personal Use Case: Grok has become my new favorite tool for researching and creating projects. One of the things that I am amazed by is its ability to be completely neutral. When I started my Night Files mystery series, I asked Grok to help me create a launch strategy for the books. Grok did that exceptionally well, then recommended Perplexity to help with the outline and strategy, and Claude to help with the writing tasks. That is a refreshing approach. I have also used it to analyze and help me choose a new TV service, saving me almost $100 per month, and to create a property tax protest, saving me almost $1500 per year. Hands down, it is one of the best research tools that I have ever worked with.

What’s New: In May 2025, Grok 3.5 improved its handling of technical queries, making it more versatile ([xAI](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=https%3A%2F%2Fx%2Eai%2Fgrok&urlhash=JYbK&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block)).

While Grok excels at real-time insights, let’s see how ChatGPT offers a broader set of skills for business tasks.

### ChatGPT: The Do-It-All Assistant

ChatGPT, from OpenAI, is the AI you’ve probably heard about. It’s like a Swiss Army knife—versatile and ready for almost anything. By June 2025, it’s added image and video generation, making it a go-to for creative projects. Its natural, conversational style feels like chatting with a trusted colleague.

* Usability: Intuitive and user-friendly, with clear responses. Score: 9/10
* Research Capabilities: Its web-browsing mode delivers detailed reports, ideal for market analysis. Score: 9/10
* Creativity: From blog posts to code, it’s a creative powerhouse. Score: 9/10
* Integration: Connects with Apple’s ecosystem and supports sharing assets, but it’s not as tied to business tools as Gemini. Score: 8/10
* Pricing: Free tier is strong, with ChatGPT Plus at $20/month for extra features ([OpenAI](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=https%3A%2F%2Fhelp%2Eopenai%2Ecom%2Fen%2Farticles%2F6825453-chatgpt-release-notes&urlhash=8pjY&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block)). Score: 8/10
* Real-Time Data Access: Solid, with web access for fresh data. Score: 9/10

Best Use Case: A marketing director writing ad copy or a developer sketching code will love ChatGPT’s flexibility.

Personal Use Case: ChatGPT has been my buddy and writing partner for almost 2.5 years now. It is where I go to write copy for my websites, book descriptions, Ad copy, and initial drafts of Non-Fiction books. While it can be frustrating at times when you want it to do something and it just won't, or you need a tweak and it changes what you were working on completely, it is a tool that I spend a large percentage of my day using. One of the new changes is that they have fixed their ability to create images. Although not the most creative (their plugin, Sola, is more creative), it works when you need a quick image.

What’s New: GPT-4o, launched in March 2025, boosts reasoning and adds Agent Mode for web tasks ([OpenAI](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=https%3A%2F%2Fhelp%2Eopenai%2Ecom%2Fen%2Farticles%2F6825453-chatgpt-release-notes&urlhash=8pjY&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block)).

ChatGPT’s versatility is impressive, but for research-heavy tasks, Perplexity takes the lead.

### Perplexity: The Data Detective

Perplexity isn’t just a chatbot—it’s a search engine with a brain. It digs deep, pulls sources, and delivers answers you can trust. By June 2025, it’s added image generation and lets Pro users compare responses from different models, making it a top pick for data-driven decisions.

* Usability: Simple interface, enhanced by the Perplexity Assistant for app-shared tasks. Score: 8/10
* Research Capabilities: The best in class, with deep web searches and Perplexity Labs reports. Score: 10/10
* Creativity: Less focused on creativity but can build dashboards or web apps. Score: 7/10
* Integration: Works on iOS, Android, and web, with cross-app support. Score: 8/10
* Pricing: Free version is robust, with Pro at $20/month for advanced tools ([TechCrunch](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftechcrunch%2Ecom%2F2025%2F05%2F29%2Fperplexitys-new-tool-can-generate-spreadsheets-dashboards-and-more%2F&urlhash=WvO5&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block)). Score: 8/10
* Real-Time Data Access: Excellent, with live data like stock prices. Score: 10/10

Best Use Case: A financial analyst tracking markets or a researcher compiling reports will rely on Perplexity’s accuracy.

Personal Use Case: I recently started using Perplexity in my Fiction writing. The tool was introduced to me by Grok. I have used it as a tool to outline and create complex plotlines, as well as plan out series of books. As an example I used it to create the entire outline of a series of 6 books that I am writing in my "Night Files" series in less than an hour. I then had it create a prompt that I could use in Claude to begin writing the series.

What’s New: Perplexity Labs, launched in May 2025, creates spreadsheets and dashboards for Pro users ([TechCrunch](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftechcrunch%2Ecom%2F2025%2F05%2F29%2Fperplexitys-new-tool-can-generate-spreadsheets-dashboards-and-more%2F&urlhash=WvO5&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block)).

Perplexity’s research strength is unmatched, but Claude offers a different approach with its focus on safety.

### Claude: The Safe and Steady Partner

Claude, from Anthropic, is the AI you trust for sensitive tasks. Its neutral tone and ethical design make it a favorite for businesses needing reliability. By June 2025, it’s gained traction for its coding skills and professional communication.

* Usability: Modern and accessible, with features like dyslexia-friendly fonts. Score: 9/10
* Research Capabilities: Strong at complex questions, with web-based insights. Score: 9/10
* Creativity: Good for documents or coding, with interactive Artifacts. Score: 8/10
* Integration: Connects to documents and offers APIs, but the integration is less seamless than Gemini. Score: 8/10
* Pricing: Free tier available, with Pro at $20/month ([Anthropic](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww%2Eanthropic%2Ecom%2Fclaude&urlhash=u2Gy&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block)). Score: 8/10
* Real-Time Data Access: Decent, but trails Grok and Perplexity. Score: 8/10

Best Use Case: A compliance officer drafting policies or a coder building secure apps will appreciate Claude’s reliability.

Personal Use Case: I recently began to write fiction again after almost 30 years. I am leveraging AI. Hands down (and I am a huge ChatGPT user) Claude is the BEST when it comes to actual writing. It is one of the most thoughtful tools and works as a real writing partner helping work out storylines and paths. As with all AI it is not perfect and will lose its way (that is why the human is running the show).

What’s New: Claude Sonnet 4 and Opus 4, released in May 2025, enhance coding and tool use ([Anthropic](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww%2Eanthropic%2Ecom%2Fclaude&urlhash=u2Gy&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block)).

Claude’s ethical focus is unique, but Gemini shines for businesses tied to Google’s ecosystem.

### Gemini: The Google-Powered Powerhouse

Gemini, from Google, is like an extension of your Google Workspace. It’s deeply integrated, making it a natural fit for businesses already using Gmail or Docs. By June 2025, it’s added tools like NotebookLM for turning notes into podcasts and Whisk and Veo for video creation.

* Usability: User-friendly, with voice and proactive features. Score: 9/10
* Research Capabilities: Deep Research mode handles complex topics well. Score: 9/10
* Creativity: Supports coding, filmmaking, and content with tools like Flow. Score: 9/10
* Integration: The best, syncing with Google Workspace and Search. Score: 10/10
* Pricing: Free tier is solid, with Google AI Pro at $19.99/month ([Google Blog](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=https%3A%2F%2Fblog%2Egoogle%2Ftechnology%2Fgoogle-deepmind%2Fgemini-model-thinking-updates-march-2025%2F&urlhash=RzyE&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block)). Score: 8/10
* Real-Time Data Access: Leverages Google Search for live data. Score: 10/10

Best Use Case: A CEO using Google Workspace for reports or market research will find Gemini’s integration unbeatable.

What’s New: Gemini 2.5 Pro and Flash, launched in March 2025, excel in reasoning and coding ([Google Blog](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=https%3A%2F%2Fblog%2Egoogle%2Ftechnology%2Fgoogle-deepmind%2Fgemini-model-thinking-updates-march-2025%2F&urlhash=RzyE&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block)).

### How They Rank

Here’s how the tools score, with an average showing their overall value:

Gemini tops the list with a 9.17 average, driven by its seamless integration. ChatGPT follows at 8.67, excelling in creativity and usability. Grok and Perplexity tie at 8.50, with strong real-time data access. Claude scores 8.33, reliable but less competitive in real-time data.

### Wrapping Up

Each AI tool offers something special. Gemini leads for businesses tied to Google, blending integration with strong performance. ChatGPT is a versatile all-rounder, perfect for creative and general tasks. Grok and Perplexity excel in real-time data, with Perplexity dominating research. Claude is a safe bet for creative writing and coding

To choose, consider your needs:

* Real-time data? Try Grok or Perplexity.
* Creative content? ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini are top picks.
* Integration? Gemini’s Google ties are unmatched.

All tools offer free versions, allowing you to test them. Paid plans, around $20/month, unlock more features. As AI evolves, keep an eye on updates to ensure you’re using the best tool for your business.

# Copilot vs. ChatGPT: Which AI chatbot should you use? [2026]

By Harry Guinness · January 7, 2026

[ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/) and [Microsoft Copilot](https://copilot.microsoft.com/) are two of the most widely available AI tools. ChatGPT is the chatbot that started the current AI boom, and Microsoft Copilot is included with Windows (the world's most popular operating system) and integrates Microsoft Office (perhaps the most famous software suite ever created). While they started as standalone conversational bots, they're both now deeply integrated with other apps, the open web, and—through your phone—even the real world.

ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot have both improved dramatically over the last few years. As their feature lists have gotten longer, drawing quick and easy comparisons between the two apps has become increasingly hard.

But I've been using both AI chatbots since they were released—and writing about them with every feature update—so I've gotten a sense of what really matters when comparing them.

Here's my take on Copilot vs. ChatGPT.

**Table of contents:**

* [Copilot vs. ChatGPT at a glance](#glance)
* [ChatGPT and Copilot are really similar](#similar)
* [ChatGPT has more advanced features](#features)
* [Copilot integrates with Microsoft's ecosystem](#microsoft)
* [ChatGPT integrates with Zapier](#zapier)
* [Both are powerful, but neither is perfect](#power)
* [You have to pay for the best features on both](#free-plans)
* [ChatGPT vs. Copilot: Which should you use?](#which)

## Copilot vs. ChatGPT at a glance

There's lots to talk about (and I will), but first, here's a quick comparison of ChatGPT and Copilot to get you started.

| **Microsoft Copilot** | **ChatGPT** |
| --- | --- |
| **Power and features** | ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ While not quite as multipurpose as ChatGPT, integration with Microsoft 365 apps is a killer feature | ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ With the latest LLMs and most advanced implementations, ChatGPT sets the bar high |
| **Availability** | ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Web and mobile apps; integration with Microsoft apps | ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Web, desktop, and mobile apps; integrates with Zapier |
| **Free plan** | ⭐️⭐️⭐️ Functional, but it lacks the integrations that make Copilot great | ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Solid, but it lacks a lot of the best features of ChatGPT |
| **Reliability** | ⭐️⭐️⭐️ I ran into some weird issues using Copilot, including one bug where it hallucinated it was ChatGPT | ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ ChatGPT can still make mistakes, but it's one of the best AI tools for reliability |

## ChatGPT and Copilot are really similar

Before diving into the *differences* between ChatGPT and Copilot, let's look at all the major ways in which they're actually really similar. They're both AI-powered productivity chatbots, and that alone means there's a lot of overlap.

Microsoft Copilot

ChatGPT

* **Both can understand and generate text, images, code, documents, and more**. These are both [multimodal](/blog/multimodal-ai/) chatbots, so if there's a feature you associate with AI chatbots, they almost certainly have it.
* **Both use the latest AI models from OpenAI**. Different models are available in both apps in a few different modes. Microsoft also claims to use [its own proprietary models](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/bing/do-more-with-ai/how-bing-chat-works?form=MA13KP), but given that it's a major investor in OpenAI and the feature overlap is so extreme, it's safe to assume that OpenAI's state-of-the-art models are doing a lot of the heavy lifting.
* **Both are available on the web and through mobile apps**. I'll get into this a little more in a bit, but you can essentially use either chatbot on any device.
* **Both apps can search the web for new information**. Gone are the days where different AI tools had different knowledge cutoff dates that affected their answers. Both ChatGPT and Copilot can pull in information from the open internet.
* **Both apps can see your screen, integrate with apps, and offer suggestions on what to do.** ChatGPT works best with text and coding apps, while Copilot works best with Windows apps, though both can also use screenshots.
* **Both apps can work with files you upload.** Add PDFs, text documents, spreadsheets, and the like, and both chatbots can help you understand them.
* **Both apps have Google Docs-like collaborative features.** ChatGPT calls it [Canvas](/blog/chatgpt-canvas/), while Copilot calls it Pages.
* **You have to pay to get the best from both apps**. While both apps have free versions, using the best and most powerful features requires you to pay upwards of $20/month.

## ChatGPT has more advanced features

OpenAI kickstarted the current AI boom, so it's no surprise that ChatGPT is packed with cutting-edge features. While there are almost too many things to list, here are some of the big areas where ChatGPT stands out from Microsoft Copilot:

* Better web and news search, including better integration with info sources for sports scores, locations, and the like.
* The ability to [create custom chatbots](/blog/custom-chatgpt/) and integrate with other apps through tools like [Zapier](https://zapier.com/).
* Other apps can now build integrations with ChatGPT, so you can control apps like Photoshop, Spotify, and Canva directly through the chat interface. (This is still in its early days yet, so it remains to be seen how useful and supported this feature is.)
* A dedicated Images section that makes it easier to [generate and edit images](/blog/chatgpt-image-generation/).
* Codex, an AI coding agent that integrates with GitHub, the terminal on your computer, and other coding tools.
* [Agent](/blog/chatgpt-agent/), an AI tool with its own browser and virtual environment that you can send off to do any task you can imagine. (Whether it succeeds or not is the big question.)

It's worth noting that ChatGPT doesn't have feature parity across all its apps. The web app tends to get features first, though the desktop and mobile apps obviously have better integrations with your devices.

Having listed all that, a lot of these features are trickling down to Copilot with time. Microsoft's deployment requirements just seem to be a little bit higher. Last year, I flagged live video in the smart phone app, file uploads, and the Google Docs-like Canvas as features that ChatGPT had that Copilot didn't. This year, Copilot has them all.

Of course, AI is moving so fast that these examples may no longer be true when you read this, but the general gist of it remains the same. ChatGPT is iterating features faster than Copilot.

## Copilot integrates with Microsoft's ecosystem

The big advantage of Microsoft Copilot is that it integrates with everything Microsoft. The Copilot app is included with Windows and is featured prominently in the taskbar. In fact, Copilot is now being pushed as the help service for a few apps, including Settings, Edge, the Windows Store, Photos, Notepad, and Paint.

The idea is you share your screen with Copilot and use your voice to tell it what you want to do. It then guides you through the apps. It worked in my testing, though I have no idea how any of the relatives I've had to do tech support for would feel about it.

Similarly, if you use Bing, there's a big Copilot button there on your home page.

If you use Edge, it's there in the sidebar ready to answer questions.

As long as you pay for Copilot Pro (for personal users) or Microsoft 365 Copilot (for businesses), you can [use Copilot across most Microsoft 365 apps](/blog/microsoft-copilot/).

For example, Copilot can:

* Summarize documents, answer questions, and generate text and images in Word and OneNote.
* Create formulas, apply formatting, and generally help out in [Excel](/blog/copilot-in-excel/).
* Generate presentation slides and summaries in PowerPoint.
* Summarize long email threads and draft replies in Outlook.

And those are just the big ones. If you live in Microsoft's ecosystem, this really is the killer feature. While ChatGPT is catching up, the integrations just aren't as easy or as deep as they are with Copilot and the Windows ecosystem.

As you dive even deeper into the enterprise version of Copilot, this distinction becomes even more relevant. While it's beyond the scope of this comparison, for multinational companies that already rely on Microsoft enterprise software, [Copilot can integrate deeply across your entire stack](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/enterprise#tabs-pill-bar-oca455_tab2). You can also [use Copilot Studio to build AI agents](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365-copilot/microsoft-copilot-studio) that integrate with your existing tools. This obviously takes some degree of institutional IT knowledge to implement, but if you're a CEO skimming this comparison, reach out to your CTO and take things from there.

## ChatGPT integrates with Zapier

ChatGPT doesn't integrate with a specific office workspace like Microsoft or Google, but it does [integrate with Zapier](https://zapier.com/apps/chatgpt/integrations), which lets you connect it to thousands of apps that you use at work. That means you can automatically generate and share content, nurture and qualify leads, summarize business information, and more—all from the apps you're already using.

If your tech stack is broad—and not focused mostly on Microsoft apps—ChatGPT's Zapier integration might be the deciding factor. It'll make AI more accessible to you in your daily work. ## Both AI chatbots are incredibly powerful, but neither is perfect for every problem

AI chatbots are in an interesting place.

For starters, it feels like some of the hype and unrealistic expectations have started to die down as AI tools haven't instantly revolutionized every area of society. After all, I'm a writer and I still have a job. But just because AI chatbots haven't matched some of the initial wild hype doesn't mean that they aren't useful.

Both ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot are capable of solving thousands of small everyday problems. They can generate drafts, translate text, pull content from images, write code, solve math problems, create recipes, and do countless other things—quickly. If you have a few tasks that you think an AI chatbot could speed up or otherwise help out with, odds are both ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot will ace it.

Plus, both have access to the same state-of-the-art models (give or take a few weeks for Copilot to catch up) so it's not as if one chatbot is miles smarter than the other.

## You have to pay for the best features on both ChatGPT and Copilot

ChatGPT and Copilot both have free plans that let you use their basic chatbot features. If you just want to generate a bad poem or answer a quick question, you can use either chatbot happily for free.

* ChatGPT's free plan offers access to more limited versions of its latest models and allows you to try out some features like image generation.
* Microsoft Copilot's free plan is available through the Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android apps, as well as the Edge browser; crucially, it doesn't work with Microsoft 365 apps like Word. There are some unspecified limits about how much you can use certain features.

Copilot maybe has the edge on the free plan as it gives you access to more features like image generation. But really, the gap between the free plans is pretty minimal for what you'd actually be using it for.

If you're serious about making the most of either tool, you'll need to pay for a premium plan.

* [ChatGPT Plus](/blog/chatgpt-plus/) is $20/month and includes all the features I've been discussing here. [ChatGPT Pro](/blog/chatgpt-pro/) is $200/month and includes unlimited access to almost all of ChatGPT's most advanced features as well as a few additional modes that use more reasoning—but it largely falls outside the scope of this comparison. ([ChatGPT Go](/blog/chatgpt-go/) is a ~$8/month plan available in some markets with lower limits than Plus.)
* Copilot comes with Microsoft 365 plans; Personal starts at $9.99/month and allows you to use Copilot in apps like Word and Outlook. (You also get access to the desktop apps as well as 1TB of cloud storage.) It's also available for business users, but pricing varies dramatically based on the number of users you have and features you need. For example, Microsoft 365 Business Standard costs $150/user/year, with Copilot costing an additional $252/user/year.

## ChatGPT vs. Copilot: Which should you use?

The consumer versions of ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot are powerful AI chatbots with a huge amount of overlapping features—the number of things one can do that the other can't is pretty small. When it comes to advanced features like AI coding agents and integrations with Microsoft Office apps, things get a little different.

Though really, deciding between them still comes down to one big question: do you use Microsoft 365 apps? Copilot's integration with Microsoft's suite of apps is a killer feature if you spend all day bouncing from PowerPoint presentations to Excel spreadsheets. If you don't rely on apps like Word, Excel, and Outlook, though, ChatGPT is the more powerful, reliable, and feature-filled tool. While the AI models are essentially the same, OpenAI has built out and deployed a lot more features than Microsoft.

And in terms of free tools, both are pretty even, but Microsoft Copilot edges it because it gives you more access to features like image generation. Even still, if you're only going to try one tool, ChatGPT is the one to go with—it's the app that created the category.

The pricing and deployment for ChatGPT Enterprise are custom-handled: unlike consumer ChatGPT (with known $20/month for Plus, etc.), Enterprise has no public list price. TechTarget notes that “no set price” is published for Enterprise; pricing is based on organization size and usage (( "Highlights: The Enterprise version, however, does,which is the tier below")). Industry reports suggest around $30/user/month is typical for ChatGPT Business (the predecessor) and Enterprise likely higher (( "Highlights: The Enterprise version, however, does,which is the tier below")). ChatGPT itself is a _cloud_ service hosted by OpenAI; no on-prem or private-cloud version is offered (though organizations can pull data via the Azure OpenAI Service if needed).

## Capabilities [...] | Feature / Aspect | ChatGPT Enterprise (OpenAI) | Claude Enterprise (Anthropic) | Microsoft Copilot | Gemini Enterprise (Google) |
 ---  --- 
| Provider | OpenAI (owned by Microsoft) | Anthropic | Microsoft (Azure + GitHub) | Google (DeepMind/Cloud) |
| Model Underlying | GPT-5.2 (flagship), GPT-5.2 Pro, GPT-5 mini/nano (( "Highlights: With its release in August,security, compliance and integration considerations")) | Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5 | Derivative of GPT-5.2 via Azure OpenAI; Code models for GitHub | Gemini 3.1 Pro (flagship), Gemini 3 Flash (fast) |
| Launch (Enterprise) | Aug 2023 | Sep 2024 | GitHub Copilot (2022); 365 Copilot (Mar 2023); Windows Copilot (2024) | Gemini Enterprise Oct 2025 | [...] In parallel, Microsoft leveraged its OpenAI partnership. It marketed GitHub Copilot (launched 2021) to developers, and in 2023 rolled out Microsoft 365 Copilot, embedding GPT-4 into Office apps. Microsoft also launched Windows Copilot (Feb 2024) and an “Azure AI Service” making OpenAI models available via Azure. By 2025, Microsoft reported generative AI in 85% of Fortune 500 through its platforms (( "Highlights: We have come a long,and customer satisfaction, according to")).
